A 72-year-old male patient seeks medical attention for neck pain that has persisted for 5 days. The
pain began after he performed overhead work changing chandelier light bulbs. He reports no pain
radiation or traumatic injury. His medical history includes atrial fibrillation treated with metoprolol.
Physical examination reveals tenderness at the right inferior aspect of the C2 spinous process, with
normal neurological findings. What is the appropriate counterstrain positioning for the neck to treat this
condition? Answer Choices: (A) neutral position with left rotation only (B) extension with bilateral
sidebending (C) pure extension without rotation (D) extension with sidebending to the left and rotation
to the right (E) extension with sidebending and rotation to the left (F) neutral flexion with bilateral
rotation (G) neutral position with right rotation only (H) flexion with sidebending and rotation to the right
(I) pure flexion without rotation (J) flexion with sidebending and rotation to the left
 A. pure extension without rotation
B. flexion with sidebending and rotation to the right
C. flexion with sidebending and rotation to the left
D. extension with bilateral sidebending
E. neutral position with left rotation only
F. neutral flexion with bilateral rotation
G. neutral position with right rotation only
H. extension with sidebending to the left and rotation to the right
I. pure flexion without rotation
J. extension with sidebending and rotation to the left
